title: Open on Paper
subtitle: Hospital Capacity Board & MCI Patient Flow

brief.userPrompt: Tuesday 20 October 2026, dusk and steady rain. The exercise starts at 17:30 in the Larkfield County Communications Center (Supervisor Keiko Tanaka) with the evening commute on Highway 21 and Larkfield Regional Medical Center (LRMC) already at 21 of 24 ED beds because of a respiratory surge; St. Brendan's Community Hospital has its CT scanner down and is on Limited intake. At 17:42 a charter bus (Tri-County Coach Lines, 31 passengers and a driver returning from a casino trip) and a fuel tanker collide near the Highway 21 and County Road K intersection; the bus is on its side against the ditch, the tanker is leaking diesel, and a small car is also involved. About 28 patients across the bus and the car are reported in the first 10 minutes; seven are trapped. Engine 3's captain takes command, declares an MCI at Level 2 and later transfers command to Battalion Chief Tom Aldrich (Battalion 1); LCEMS Deputy Chief Luis Navarro becomes Medical Group Supervisor. Pressure points: the county uses START and JumpSTART while the coalition is moving to SALT and the Medical Director may order SALT, so the method must be stated on the radio; the triage pass should finish in 15 to 20 minutes and the counts of Immediate, Delayed, Minor and Expectant patients must agree between command, the PIO and the hospitals; LRMC has 3 trauma bays and takes at most 3 Immediate patients in the first 30 minutes, so further Immediate patients go to St. Brendan's, or by Air 7 to Lakeshore University Medical Center (Level I, burn center) for head and burn injuries; Minor patients go by Larkfield County Transit bus to the Brandt Lake High School minor injury site, not to hospitals; walking wounded leave in private cars and arrive at Pinecrest Memorial unannounced; the hospital capacity board shows a hospital opened to arrivals that is actually on Diversion; at 18:20 a firefighter is hurt when the bus shifts during extrication and calls a mayday, the RIT is committed and a personnel accountability report is taken; the tank leak requires diking and the state natural resources agency; the dispatcher must manage three radio channels plus MED 1 and mutual aid ambulances from two neighboring counties; the Medical Examiner is notified when the first patient is tagged deceased; the reunification center at Brandt Lake High School opens with the Red Cross and a call-in line; social media posts give a casualty count of 40 that differs from command's 28; families call the hospitals. Decisions the exercise should record: MCI declaration, triage method, triage complete report with counts, patient destination assignments with reasons and mode, hospital open or diversion status changes, mutual aid requests, command transfer, accountability reports, and public statements with the casualty count stated. The SimCell plays the hospitals' MEDCOM nurses, the coalition coordinator, the air medical crews, neighboring EMS agencies, the State Patrol, the Medical Examiner, the Red Cross, the bus company, the fuel company, families and reporters.
audience: Medical Group Supervisor / Triage and Transportation Leaders
constraints: Every county email address uses the exercise domain larkfieldcountywi.example; hospitals use lrmc-exercise.example and similar; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real agency, company, hospital or newspaper domain.

All patients are synthetic with no real names or real medical record numbers; triage tags use START or SALT categories (Immediate, Delayed, Minor, Expectant, Deceased) consistent with the vitals on the patient list; the patient list and the transport log have monotonic times; times are Central Daylight Time.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the air medical crews, neighboring EMS, the State Patrol, the Medical Examiner, the Red Cross, the bus company, the fuel company, other hospitals' staff, families and reporters are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Trust in hospital status data when the capacity board and a key scanner fail. Getting patients to the right hospital under hard bed limits. Keeping command, accountability and the casualty count on the radio and in public statements the same across all three.
overview.threat: Before STARTEX, St. Brendan's Community Hospital's CT scanner failed, so the hospital went to Limited intake. LRMC was already at 21 of 24 ED beds because of a respiratory surge. At 17:42 on Tuesday 20 October 2026, at dusk in steady rain, a Tri-County Coach Lines charter bus (31 passengers and a driver) and a fuel tanker collide near the Highway 21 and County Road K intersection, and a small car is also involved. The bus ends up on its side against the ditch, the tanker leaks diesel, about 28 patients are reported and seven are trapped. During the MCI, the hospital capacity board (the shared web page that LRMC MEDCOM keeps) shows one hospital as open to arrivals when it is actually on Diversion. This breaks the destination rules, MEDCOM's status reports, transport decisions, hospital surge planning and the public casualty count that all rely on the board.
overview.operationalImpact: At the scene, firefighters and company officers extricate seven trapped patients from a bus lying on its side. Hazmat technicians dike a diesel leak in the rain while EMS waits in the cold zone until fire declares the scene safe. Triage crews have to state on the radio whether they are using START/JumpSTART or SALT, which the Medical Director may order. They should finish the triage pass in 15 to 20 minutes and report counts of Immediate, Delayed, Minor and Expectant patients. At 18:20 the bus shifts during extrication and a hurt firefighter calls a mayday. The channel is cleared, the RIT is committed and a PAR follows, while patient care continues under a second command position. In the treatment areas, Immediate patients wait because LRMC can take only 3 in the first 30 minutes. Others need routing to St. Brendan's, where the CT is down and intake is limited, or by Air 7 to Lakeshore for head and burn injuries. The Transportation Unit Leader cannot trust the board: one hospital shown as open is actually on Diversion, so an ambulance may be sent to the wrong door. Minor patients wait for Larkfield County Transit buses to the Brandt Lake High School minor injury site. Walking wounded leave in private cars and arrive unannounced at Pinecrest Memorial, which has only 5 ED beds. Telecommunicators handle LARK DISP 1, LARK CMD 2, LARK TAC 3 and MED 1 while mutual aid ambulances from two neighboring counties check in. Social media reports 40 casualties against command's 28. Families call hospitals that will not give out names, and the reunification center line and the PIO face pressure to state one count that matches.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to assign and log a destination for every tagged patient under SOP-MC-02 4 (no more than 3 Immediate patients to LRMC in the first 30 minutes, no more than one-third of Delayed patients to any one hospital, Air 7 to Lakeshore for head and burn injuries, and Minor patients by bus to Brandt Lake High School), even when St. Brendan's has Limited intake because its CT is down.

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to spot that the LRMC MEDCOM capacity board shows a hospital as open when it is on Diversion, to confirm each hospital's real status by voice on MED 1, and to stop or redirect any ambulance already sent to the wrong door.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to keep command, the mayday and the personnel accountability report on LARK CMD 2 and LARK TAC 3 when the bus shifts at 18:20, while the Medical Group keeps triage, treatment and transport going under a second command position and dispatch logs every change in CAD.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to release one casualty count, approved by the IC and confirmed with MEDCOM, through a Joint Information Center within 45 minutes, against social media reports of 40 casualties, and to send families to the Brandt Lake High School reunification center and call-in line instead of the hospitals.

roles.name: Incident Commander (Battalion 1, Fire Battalion Chief)
roles.team: Team A: Incident Commander / Fire Battalion Chief
roles.description: Owns overall strategy at the Highway 21 and County Road K crash: takes command from the first-arriving company officer with a full briefing, declares the MCI, decides when the scene is safe for EMS, runs the mayday and the personnel accountability report, and approves every casualty count released.
standingOrders: Safety First: EMS stays in the cold zone until fire declares the bus and the diesel leak safe, even while patients are waiting.
Mayday Priority: if a mayday is called, clear the channel, commit the RIT and get a personnel accountability report, but let patient flow continue under a named second command position.
One Number: no casualty count leaves the command post until you have approved it and MEDCOM has confirmed it, however hard the media and the families push.
Ask Early: request mutual aid ambulances and state resources early, because the units arrive a few at a time.

roles.name: Medical Group Supervisor (Triage and Transportation Leaders)
roles.team: Team B: Medical Group Supervisor / Triage and Transportation Leaders
roles.description: Manages triage, treatment, transportation and medical communications at the scene (usually Deputy Chief Luis Navarro or the on-duty shift supervisor), including the triage method, the counts in each category and every destination decision.
standingOrders: Name the Method: state on the radio whether crews are using START/JumpSTART or SALT, and change it only when the Medical Director orders it.
Injury Over Distance: the destination follows the injury and the hospital's confirmed status, not which hospital is nearest.
Verify the Board: if the capacity board and the voice on MED 1 disagree, trust the voice and hold or redirect the ambulance.
No Tag, No Transport: log tag number, priority, hospital, mode, time and reason before any ambulance leaves.

roles.name: Dispatch Supervisor (Telecommunicator)
roles.description: Manages LARK DISP 1, LARK CMD 2, LARK TAC 3 and MED 1, assigns units, announces and records command transfers in CAD, and handles mutual aid check-in and the call load across the rest of the county.
standingOrders: Channel Discipline: keep hospital traffic on MED 1 and tactical traffic on LARK TAC 3, and clear the channel at once for emergency traffic.
Record Everything: log every command transfer, mayday and unit status change in CAD with the time.
Cover the County: keep units back for the rest of the county even when the scene asks for more.

roles.name: LRMC MEDCOM Nurse (Hospital Medical Communications Coordinator)
roles.team: Team D: Hospital Medical Communications (MEDCOM) Nurse
roles.description: Manages the hospital capacity board and the hospital side of MED 1: gets and confirms each hospital's status, accepts or refuses offered patients, and reports the counts of arriving patients.
standingOrders: Trust but Confirm: treat any board entry older than 30 minutes, or one that does not match a phone call, as unconfirmed until a hospital contact confirms it by voice.
Say It Plainly: announce Diversion and Limited intake on MED 1 in plain words, not only on the web page.
Respect the Bays: do not accept more than 3 Immediate patients to LRMC in the first 30 minutes, whatever the pressure from the scene.

roles.name: Larkfield Healthcare Coalition Coordinator
roles.description: Manages the regional view of beds, Diversion, surge plans, inpatient transfers and patient tracking across LRMC, St. Brendan's, Pinecrest and Lakeshore.
standingOrders: Whole Region: watch every hospital's load, including Pinecrest's 5 ED beds and the walking wounded arriving by private car.
Surge Before Saturation: push hospitals to start their surge plans and move LRMC inpatients to Lakeshore before the ED beds run out.
Close the Gap: tell MEDCOM and the Medical Group as soon as a hospital's real status differs from the board.

roles.name: Public Information Officer (LCEMS PIO Sandra Kowal)
roles.description: Owns the public message, the Joint Information Center, the released casualty count and family reunification guidance through the Brandt Lake High School gymnasium and the call-in line.
standingOrders: Approved Counts Only: release only counts the IC has approved and MEDCOM has confirmed, and always say the number may change.
Truth Over Speed: correct the social media figure of 40 with what has been confirmed; do not guess or reassure beyond the facts.
Families to Reunification: send families to the reunification center and call-in line 920-555-0195, never to the hospitals.

phases.title: Rain, Diesel, Stale Data
phases.goal: Tests the first size-up, MCI declaration and command setup, and whether MEDCOM and the Transportation Unit Leader notice early that the LRMC MEDCOM capacity board is not updating. Also tests keeping command and the mayday on LARK CMD 2 and LARK TAC 3 while the Medical Group keeps working.
beats: (17:42–17:55) 911 calls report the Tri-County Coach Lines bus on its side at Highway 21 and County Road K with a diesel-leaking tanker and a small car. The first-arriving company officer gives a size-up under BLFD 3. The first EMS crew declares 'Larkfield, MCI declared, estimated 28 patients, Level 2' under the LCEMS MCI plan 2. Dispatch repeats it on all channels and opens the CAD incident. Command passes to Battalion 1 with a briefing and the time is logged. Hazmat dikes the diesel and EMS waits in the cold zone until fire declares the scene safe.

(18:00) The Medical Director names the triage method (START with JumpSTART for the children, or SALT), and Triage must state it on LARK TAC 3. The Medical Communications Coordinator calls LRMC MEDCOM on MED 1 under LCEMS MCI plan 6. MEDCOM reads the board: LRMC Open at 21/24 ED beds, St. Brendan's Limited intake (CT down), Pinecrest Open, Lakeshore Open via Air 7.
Noise: a routine cardiac-arrest call in the Station 2 / Pell Harbor Road district waits in the pending queue because units are committed to the MCI. Dispatch has to decide on coverage.

(18:10) MEDCOM nurse notices that Pinecrest Memorial's row on the capacity board shows a 'last updated' time of 16:55, and the board's auto-refresh fails with an error. The hospital's status push did not update and no one has received a fallback phone or fax status. The first walking wounded are already driving to Pinecrest, which has 5 ED beds.

(18:20) The bus shifts during extrication and an injured firefighter calls a mayday three times on LARK TAC 3. Battalion 1 clears the channel, commits the RIT and orders a PAR on LARK CMD 2. The Medical Group continues triage, treatment and transport under a second command position, and dispatch logs each change in CAD.

phases.title: The Wrong Door
phases.goal: Tests whether the players see that the board is wrong, confirm each hospital's real status by voice on MED 1, and stop or redirect an ambulance sent to a hospital on Diversion. Also tests whether they hold one casualty count while the failure spreads to transport decisions and public statements.
beats: (18:35) PAR complete, firefighter transported. Triage pass reported: counts of Immediate, Delayed, Minor and Expectant patients total 28. LRMC has taken its 3 Immediate patients for the first 30 minutes under SOP-MC-02 4. A mutual aid ambulance from a neighboring county is assigned a Delayed patient to Pinecrest because the board shows it Open.

(18:50) Pinecrest charge nurse (SimCell) calls MEDCOM. Pinecrest went on Diversion at 18:15 after unannounced walk-ins filled its 5 ED beds, but the board still shows Open. The mutual aid ambulance is 6 minutes out on Highway 21. The Transportation Unit Leader and MEDCOM must stop or redirect it and log the change.

Red herring: LRMC IT (SimCell) suggests the board 'may have been tampered with' after a phishing alert earlier in the day. Some players want to treat it as a cyber incident and shut the board down. Others blame the rain-related network outage at Pinecrest. The alarm history shows the status-sync service stopped at 16:55, before the crash.
Visual for the room: a screenshot of the capacity board, all four hospitals green, next to MEDCOM's handwritten voice roll call showing St. Brendan's Limited intake and Pinecrest on Diversion.

(19:05) A social media post with a photo of the bus claims '40 casualties'. A reporter calls the PIO. The count must be approved by the IC and confirmed with MEDCOM and released through a Joint Information Center, and families must be sent to the Brandt Lake High School reunification center (LCDERF 6). The board vendor (SimCell) says it will be restored in 30 minutes, and nobody believes it.

phases.title: Board Off, Voice On
phases.goal: Tests the one high-consequence call: whether to stop using the capacity board and run all destinations by voice roll call on MED 1, or keep using the degraded board with spot checks. Also tests running the manual workaround and the friction with partners that it brings.
beats: DECISION POINT (19:35): MEDCOM, the Coalition Coordinator and the Medical Group Supervisor must decide. One option is to declare the capacity board unreliable and switch every destination to a voice roll call on MED 1 every 15 minutes. That slows transports, ties up MED 1 and MEDCOM staff, and patients still on scene wait longer. The other option is to keep dispatching off the board and spot-check by phone, which risks another wrong-door transport for a patient who is already deteriorating.

The manual workaround needs people: a second MEDCOM nurse and a scribe for the paper status board, a hospital liaison at each ED, and the Coalition Coordinator calling hospitals for bed counts. Dispatch posts the hospital statuses on the unit status board, and the Transportation Unit Leader keeps a paper transport log (time, tag, priority, unit, ground/air, destination, reason).

Partner friction: St. Brendan's (Limited intake, CT down) refuses a head-injury patient. Air 7 (SimCell) has one helicopter and a 25-minute turnaround to Lakeshore in rain and low ceilings. LRMC is near its 8-Delayed-in-the-first-hour limit and asks the coalition to transfer inpatients to Lakeshore under SOP-MC-02 5.

Minor patients still wait for Larkfield County Transit buses to the Brandt Lake High School minor injury site. The Red Cross reports the reunification line is overloaded with families calling about passengers whose names the hospitals will not give out.

Media pressure with a deadline (20:00): the regional TV station (SimCell) will air the '40 casualties' figure on the 20:00 broadcast unless the JIC gives one confirmed count. The count must match the tag count, patient list and MEDCOM's hospital arrival totals.

phases.title: Trust, but Verify
phases.goal: Tests a phased return to the restored capacity board with verification before it is trusted. Also tests matching every product's count and making the required notifications before ENDEX.
beats: (20:35) The vendor and LRMC IT report the status-sync service restarted. The board comes back in order: LRMC first, then Lakeshore, then St. Brendan's and Pinecrest. Players must decide whether to run the board and the voice roll call side by side before going back to the board alone.

Hurdle (20:50): Pinecrest's row returns showing 'Open' again because its status interface uses a cached value. The fix needs a vendor engineer on site, who is 3 hours away. Pinecrest stays on voice-only status, and St. Brendan's CT repair part will not arrive until tomorrow, so it stays at Limited intake.

Verification: MEDCOM compares each hospital row against a voice confirmation on MED 1 and the 15-minute door counts under SOP-MC-02 4. The Transportation Unit Leader checks that every tag has a logged destination and that no hospital got more than it said it could take.

Count reconciliation: the tag count, patient list, transport log, hospital arrival totals (including walk-ins at Pinecrest) and the PIO's released number must agree. Any difference must be explained before the JIC's final update and the LarkfieldAlert road-closure lift for Highway 21.

(21:20) Notifications: the Coalition Coordinator updates Wisconsin Emergency Management, DNR closes out the diesel spill, and the Medical Examiner is notified of any Deceased. An after-action note records the board failure timeline (status sync stopped 16:55) and the wrong-door transport, then ENDEX at 21:30.

metrics.fail: Players do not cite plan sections. MED sends a fourth Immediate to LRMC within 30 minutes at I-06, routes the head-injury patient at I-12 by distance rather than to Lakeshore, or transports Minor patients to hospitals.

metrics.excellence: MEDCOM restates the SOP-MC-02 4 limits (3 Immediate to LRMC in 30 minutes, one-third of Delayed per hospital, 8 Delayed to LRMC) at I-02 and tracks them on the paper board before I-12 forces it. objectiveCapabilities.why: The Medical Group has to apply the SOP-MC-02 4 destination rules to every tagged patient: the Immediate cap at LRMC, the spread of Delayed patients, routing by injury to Lakeshore by Air 7 and Minor patients by bus. It must do this while St. Brendan's is on Limited intake, and log each decision.

MEDCOM and the Coalition Coordinator have to see that the capacity board is stale. They must rebuild each hospital's real status and door count from the hospital contacts so the Medical Group gets accurate, decision-ready information.
With the board down, status is confirmed by voice on MED 1. The radio plan has to keep MED 1 free for hospital traffic so a wrong-door ambulance can be redirected in time.
The IC has to run the mayday, the RIT and the PAR, and name a second command position so the Medical Group keeps patient flow going. The command transfer and mayday times must be logged.
Dispatch has to clear the channel for emergency traffic and keep command, tactical and medical traffic on their assigned channels (LARK CMD 2, LARK TAC 3, MED 1) during the mayday.

The PIO has to open the JIC, release only the count the IC has approved and MEDCOM has confirmed, correct the figure of 40, and send families to the Brandt Lake High School reunification center and the call-in line.
Releasing one count means the IC, MEDCOM and the PIO have to agree on the approval, and the PIO cannot release before that happens.

hotwash.methodDescription: 3-Up, 3-Down: ask the room for three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room one team at a time (Command, Medical Group/Transportation, MEDCOM, Dispatch, hospitals, PIO/JIC), write each item on the whiteboard in two columns, and don't allow debate until every team has spoken.

questions.text: At 18:10 (I-03), the capacity board showed Pinecrest OPEN with 5 beds. The data was last updated at 16:55, a red 'status feed timeout' banner was across the top, and no one from Pinecrest had called. Two minutes later the Pinecrest clerk's voicemail said walk-ins were arriving and 'nobody called us.' At what moment did you stop trusting the board? Who made that call out loud, and how long did it take to get a voice roll call on MED 1? Then at 18:58 (I-08), the page reload turned every row green with 'Last updated: --' and the banner was gone. Did anyone read that as recovery? If so, what told you it wasn't?

At 19:35 (I-11), the StatusGrid engineer said the restart had failed with exit code 1067 and the board was wrong for both Pinecrest and St. Brendan's. At the same time, Transportation had LC-0412, just upgraded to Immediate, loaded on Tamarack Medic 12 with a tablet showing St. Brendan's Open. Did the vendor's technical report change what MEDCOM told the field, and did the field understand what 'StatusSync dropped' meant for them? What did you tell Medic 12, how long did that take, and was Medic 41's earlier trip toward Pinecrest ever stopped, redirected or logged as a poor-fit destination?

Between 19:52 and 19:56 (I-12), the constraints piled up. St. Brendan's refused LC-0421, the head injury with a deficit. Air 7 could not be back at the LZ until 20:20. LRMC had taken 7 of its 8 allowed Delayed patients. Using SOP-MC-02 section 4, walk through where LC-0421 and your remaining Immediates and Delayed patients actually went, and whether each destination was logged with tag, priority, hospital, mode and reason. Did anyone ask the coalition to start the section 5 inpatient transfer from LRMC to Lakeshore before LRMC threatened to go to Limited intake at 20:30? What would have let you decide sooner?

At 19:45 (I-11b), the LRMC House Supervisor could spare only one float nurse for 90 minutes and no liaisons for the other hospitals. Two minutes later the Oxbow County duty officer complained that your status roll calls were blocking MED 1 and asked who had the transport log. While the bus shift at 18:20 was being worked, how did you keep command, mayday and PAR traffic on LARK CMD 2 and TAC 3, separate from the Medical Group's MED 1 traffic? Who owned the backup paper board? Did hospital statuses and every change get into CAD and onto the unit status board where mutual aid crews could see them?

At 18:22 to 18:25 (I-04b), @BrandtLakeBackroads had a post claiming 40+ hurt and a MAYDAY, with families heading to LRMC, and Channel 9 News was going live at 18:30 asking for a number and a hospital. What did you tell the public before you knew the real count? Who approved it, and was it checked with MEDCOM even though the board was stale? Did the Joint Information Center release one count within 45 minutes and send families to the Brandt Lake High School reunification center and call-in line rather than LRMC? Do the scene triage count, hospital door counts (including Pinecrest's walk-ins) and public count agree now? If not, how will the after action report explain the difference?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: StatusGrid Health Systems on-call engineer (capacity board vendor, support@statusgrid.example). Also play the partners that depend on the board: the Oxbow County EMS duty officer and the Tamarack Medic 12 crew, whose MDT tablets show the board.
simcellScripts.trigger: MEDCOM, the coalition coordinator or LRMC IT calls StatusGrid about the stale board or the 'Auto-refresh failed' banner, or a mutual aid crew asks Dispatch why its tablet shows all four hospitals Open (from I-03 onward; scripted calls at I-09b, I-11, I-16 and I-17).
hardQuestions: Engineer: "What's your support ticket number? I can't touch a production server without a ticket and a signed remote-access request from your IT on-call. Who at LRMC is authorizing this?"
Engineer: "Did anybody change anything on your side since our 14:12 maintenance? Do you have the server alarm history saved, or did someone reboot it and wipe the log?"

Oxbow duty officer: "My medics can't hear their patch traffic because you're reading statuses on MED 1. Put hospital status on your unit status board where my MDTs can see it. And who has the transport log? Medic 41 wants proof it was told to go to Pinecrest."

Engineer, when asked for a guarantee: "I can try again at 19:50, but I'm not promising anything. If you want to stop relying on the board, that's your clinical call, not mine. My job is to get it running again."
concessions: Gives a firm restart window and explains the 16:55 replay risk, but only after MEDCOM gives a ticket number and LRMC IT sends a written remote-access approval.

Purges the replay queue before the 20:33 restart, and confirms that Pinecrest needs an on-site engineer (Milwaukee, about midnight), only if MEDCOM tells him the hospitals are flashing old values and asks for a row-by-row check.

Oxbow duty officer stops complaining once Dispatch gives a set time for the MED 1 roll call (for example every 15 minutes) and names who holds the transport log with Medic 41's 18:36 and 18:52 entries.

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: Pinecrest Memorial Hospital charge nurse, Wausau Road (critical access, 5 ED beds, one doctor)
simcellScripts.trigger: Anyone at MEDCOM, the coalition or the Medical Group calls Pinecrest to confirm status or offer a patient, or MEDCOM returns the cut-off 18:12 voicemail (I-03, I-07, I-17).
hardQuestions: "I faxed our Diversion at 18:15. Who reads that fax? Why is your board still telling ambulances to come here?"
"I've got nine walk-ins from your bus with no tags. Are they in your 28 or not? Who do I report them to, and how often?"
"Your board says Open again at 20:47. Who checked that with me before your crews started trusting it?"
"Families are at my front desk asking for names. Are you sending them here, or to the high school? Someone needs to tell me what to say."
concessions: Agrees to report the door count to MEDCOM every 15 minutes by voice on a set schedule, once MEDCOM names a single contact and puts Pinecrest on voice-only status.

Gives a breakdown of the walk-ins (age, sex, rough priority, no names) that the coalition can match against the manifest, if the coalition asks for it through patient tracking and not through the media.
Will reopen to Minor transfers only after her supervisor approves and MEDCOM confirms by voice. She will not accept a board-only offer.

simcellScripts.trigger: The IC or Hazmat reports the diesel release (it passed 25 gallons by 18:30, per Brandt Lake Fire Department SOP section 4), or the coalition sends the state its count. If no one reports the spill by 19:30, DNR calls the IC.
hardQuestions: DNR: "Your crews had over 25 gallons on the ground by 18:30. Why am I hearing about it now? What time did the release start, and when was the source plugged?"
DNR: "Is the storm drain covered? Did any fuel reach the outfall? Who is the responsible party: the tanker carrier or the fuel company? Who signs for the fire department?"
WEM duty officer: "I need your final patient count and hospital status for the state log. Does it match the field and the hospital reports? If not, tell me why in writing."
WEM duty officer: "You're Level 2. Are you asking for state resources through the coalition or not? I can't log a request nobody made."
concessions: DNR will close the spill report once it has a signed fire department statement (about 40 gallons, plugged 19:15, drain covered) and the contractor's absorbent pickup is confirmed.

WEM will accept one reconciled count with a short note explaining the gap (9 untagged walk-ins at Pinecrest, the tanker driver who drove himself, LC-0417's double entry) if it comes from the coalition coordinator Greg Wilmot.
WEM gives a direct callback number for any request for state resources once the coalition confirms the request with the IC's approval.

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Players are evaluated on how plans, procedures and coordination work, not on individual performance.

The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the weather, patient counts, hospital statuses and capacity board behavior as written and do not argue with the scenario.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, including the LCEMS MCI Plan, SOP-MC-02, the LCDERF and the Brandt Lake Fire Department technical rescue guidance. Where a plan is silent, players say what they would do and name the gap.
Players have only the information in the module narrative and the injects delivered to them. Facts that come out later in the exercise are not available earlier.

**Module 2: The Wrong Door (18:30–19:30)**

It is 18:30. It is dark and still raining at 44°F.

At 17:42, CAD 26-118342 came in: a Tri-County Coach Lines charter bus on its side in the east ditch at Highway 21 and County Road K, after hitting a fuel tanker. A passenger car is also involved. Engine 3 established Highway 21 Command and declared a **Level 2 MCI with an estimated 28 patients**. Battalion 1 arrived at 17:58. The Medical Director ordered county START, with JumpSTART for children.

At 18:01, MEDCOM read the board:
- LRMC: Open, 21 of 24 ED beds full, 3 trauma bays
- St. Brendan's: Limited intake, no head injuries
- Pinecrest: Open, 5 ED beds
- Lakeshore: Open, Immediate patients by Air 7 only

At 18:10, a red banner appeared on the board: **"Auto-refresh failed... Data shown may be stale."** The Pinecrest row still shows a last update of 16:55. At 18:12, a Pinecrest ED clerk left a voicemail that was cut off partway, saying walk-ins from the crash were arriving and "nobody called us."

At 18:20, Firefighter Kowalczyk called a **MAYDAY** on LARK TAC 3. The bus shifted off its struts and pinned his leg at the rear hatch. He is still pinned, the RIT is cutting him free, and five patients remain trapped. About 35 gallons of diesel have been diked at the storm drain. Five mutual aid ambulances are checking in at staging, and CAD shows 9 pending calls. A post with 310 shares claims "40+ hurt." Channel 9 News has just gone live with "40 injured and a firefighter trapped." The red banner is still showing, and nobody has called Pinecrest back.

**Module 3: Board Off, Voice On (19:30–20:30)**

It is 19:30. It is dark, with steady rain at 43°F and a low cloud ceiling.

At 18:50, the Pinecrest charge nurse called to say Pinecrest has been on **Diversion since 18:15**. Its ED is full of walk-ins from the crash who came by private car, but the board still showed it Open. Oxbow Medic 41, which had been sent to Pinecrest, was redirected to St. Brendan's at 18:52. A page reload at 18:58 turned all four board rows green with no update times. MEDCOM's handwritten voice roll call on MED 1 shows the real picture: LRMC trauma bays full; St. Brendan's on Limited intake (CT down); Pinecrest on Diversion; Lakeshore taking Immediate patients by Air 7 only.

LRMC IT emailed that a phishing email was clicked that morning and suggested shutting the board down. The StatusGrid vendor engineer says the status service failed and a remote fix is due at 19:50. A Tamarack crew reports that its tablet shows all four hospitals Open.

Kowalczyk is in the LRMC ED, and the Rescue Group PAR is complete. Scene triage: **28 patients** (7 Immediate, 9 Delayed, 11 Minor, 1 Expectant). Still on scene: 3 Immediate, 1 Delayed, 4 Minor and the Expectant patient, and one patient is still trapped. LRMC opened its surge ward at 19:10. CAD shows 11 pending calls, and Channel 9 News keeps repeating "40 injured."

**Module 4: Trust, but Verify (20:30–21:30)**

It is 20:30. It is dark, the rain is easing and it is 42°F.

**Rescue and transport.** The last trapped patient was cut free at 19:58 and went to LRMC after voice confirmation on MED 1. All groups gave a PAR at 20:05, and every member is accounted for. LC-0412, upgraded to Immediate, went to St. Brendan's at 19:38 after voice confirmation. Air 7 lifted head injury LC-0421 to Lakeshore at 20:24. The last 4 Minor patients are loading onto the second transit bus.

**Deceased patient.** At 20:22, after reassessment approved by the Medical Director, the Expectant patient, LC-0428, was found to have no signs of life and is now tagged **Deceased**. He is covered in place, and a paramedic stays with him.

**Fuel spill.** The diesel source was plugged at 19:15. About 40 gallons have been diked and absorbed at the storm drain.

**Hospitals.** LRMC went to Limited intake at 20:30 (Immediate patients by voice only) and has moved 2 stable inpatients to Lakeshore. Pinecrest is still on Diversion. St. Brendan's remains on Limited intake. The paper board on the MEDCOM whiteboard is the only status everyone trusts, and the vendor is still working on the capacity board.

**Counts.** The scene is almost clear, but the hospitals, the transport log, the reunification center and Channel 9 News each have a different number. CAD shows 13 pending calls. This module covers the return to normal operations, matching the counts and the required notifications before ENDEX.
